title: Psychometric Question Bank (V2 Sample)
instruction_user_facing: Pick the option that is most like what you would actually do.
structure: Reduced demo bank: 15 traits × 1 item each (15 total questions). One representative item per trait.
note: Public reduced demo bank (15 questions total). No answer key included.

items.prompt: You notice a small mismatch in your daily records.

options.A: Mark it and continue; you will reconcile it later.
options.B: Re-check the last step before sending anything out.
options.C: Assume it is normal variation and keep going.
options.D: Ask someone if they have seen the same issue.

traits.trait_description: acts fast without thinking; higher score = more self-regulated

items.prompt: A “today-only” deal pops up while you are tired. 1

options.A: Buy now, but keep it within a strict limit.
options.B: Add it to cart and decide tomorrow.
options.C: Buy now; you can adjust later if needed.
options.D: Close it and check your budget before deciding.

items.prompt: A loan term is unclear but the process is moving fast.

options.A: Sign and learn later; speed matters.
options.C: Ask until you feel comfortable enough to explain it back.
options.D: Ask a friend later and decide after that.

items.prompt: You can earn more this week, but it may create a problem next month.

options.A: Take the extra earnings now and handle later.
options.B: Take it only if you can still cover next month.
options.C: Choose stability even if it means less now.
options.D: Take it and hope it works out.

items.prompt: You promised yourself “no borrowing this month,” but a temptation appears.

options.A: Borrow a small amount; it won’t matter.
options.B: Borrow if the reason feels justified.
options.C: Try to adjust spending first, then decide.
options.D: Stick to the rule unless it is a true emergency.

items.prompt: A plan fails and you lose time.

options.B: There is always something you can change next time.
options.C: It was unavoidable; nothing could help. 4
options.D: Partly luck, partly choices; you can adjust.

items.prompt: You can slightly exaggerate income and likely benefit.

options.A: Adjust it upward; everyone does it.
options.B: Adjust it a little if it helps.
options.C: Report honestly, but round if needed and explain.
options.D: Avoid giving a number and let them decide.

items.prompt: Someone suggests a “small gift” to speed a process.

options.B: Accept only if you are truly stuck.
options.C: Avoid if possible and look for normal options.
options.D: Refuse and use the proper process.

items.prompt: Payment is due today but you are short.

options.B: Pay what you can and communicate a clear plan early.
options.D: Pay partially and hope they understand.
Pause for a while and see later.

items.prompt: You can get 100 today or 130 next month.

options.B: Take next month unless you urgently need today.
options.C: Take today, but only if you planned for it.

traits.trait_description: calibrated risk; higher score = better risk management

options.C: Choose based on your buffer and obligations.
options.D: Choose gamble when you feel confident.

items.prompt: Two loans: one low monthly, one low total.

options.A: Choose the one with the lowest monthly payment.
options.B: Choose the one with the lowest total cost and manageable risk.
options.C: Choose the one that feels simpler.

options.A: Spend it; extra money is for life.
options.B: Save first, then decide on a small treat.
options.D: Spend most now; saving can start later.

items.prompt: You promised delivery Friday; work becomes harder midweek.

options.B: Inform early and propose a realistic plan.
